entities.summary:
Pope Callixtus III, born Alonso de Borja, but referred to in English-language accounts as Alfonso de Borgia as a member of the House of Borgia, was head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from 8 April 1455 to his death, in August 1458.

    As Pope, he played a key role in the Pazzi conspiracy against the Medicis, a powerful Florentine family, which ultimately led to the downfall of the Medicis' influence in Florence. The conspiracy, however, also led to the rise of the powerful Lorenzo de' Medici, who would go on to play a significant role in the Italian Renaissance.

    Callixtus III's papacy was marked by the ongoing conflict between the Catholic Church and the Ottoman Empire, which had been expanding its territories in Eastern Europe and the Middle East. The Pope's efforts to negotiate with the Ottomans were largely unsuccessful, and the empire continued to pose a significant threat to European Christianity.

    Despite these challenges, Callixtus III is remembered for his efforts to reform the Catholic Church and reduce corruption within its ranks. He also oversaw the construction of several major churches and monasteries, including the Basilica of St. Peter in Rome.

    The Pope's legacy is also marked by his role in the development of the Sistine Chapel, which was built during his papacy and features some of Michelangelo's most famous works, including the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pope Callixtus III played a significant role in the Italian Renaissance, as his papacy marked the beginning of the end of the Pazzi conspiracy and the rise of Lorenzo de' Medici, who would go on to shape the course of European history.
